question: The Commission enjoys broad support in screening the EU acquis for overlaps and inconsistencies. Simplification is essential, especially where EU legislation complicates permitting procedures for businesses and farmers. Initiatives to simplify permitting under the Clean Industrial Deal, the Affordable Energy Action Plan and the Defence Readiness Omnibus are welcome steps.

Despite their legitimate objectives, EU environmental laws often remain a practical obstacle to sustainable development, legal certainty and investment, particularly in densely populated and fragmented regions. A pragmatic approach is needed to ensure legal certainty, economic development and competitiveness, without questioning environmental objectives.
A call for a simplification package for environmental legislation with a major impact on permitting procedures is therefore justified.

Evaluation of, inter alia, the Habitats Directive1, the Birds Directive2, the Nature Restoration Regulation3, the Water Framework Directive4 and the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive5 is desirable, with attention paid to socioeconomic consequences and disproportionate effects on businesses and agriculture. 1.
Does the Commission intend to present a simplification package for environmental legislation with a substantial impact on agriculture and businesses? If so, what are the timeline and approach?
Is the Commission willing to evaluate the abovementioned directives and regulations with a view to simplification, including greater scope for socio-economic considerations in permitting?

Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, pp. 7, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/1992/43/oj. Directive 2009/147/EC of 30 November 2009 on the conservation of wild birds, OJ L 20, 26.1.2010, pp. 7, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2009/147/oj.

answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.9.2025) The Competitiveness Compass for the EU1 sets the target of cutting administrative burden by at least 25% for all companies and at least 35% for small and medium-sized enterprises without undermining the respective policy goals. Making rules easier and cheaper to implement also contributes to preserving environmental goals.

As mentioned in its Single Market Strategy2, the Commission intends to present in autumn 2025 a proposal to reduce administrative burden linked to environmental laws. The Commission consulted stakeholders on the initiative, through a Call for Evidence3 published on 22 July and with a feedback period until 10 September 2025.

The specific content of the future proposal will be decided on after consideration of the responses to the consultation. In any event, the initiative aims to simplify and streamline administrative requirements related to the environment in the areas of waste, products, and industrial emissions. The initiative may also consider permitting challenges relating to environmental assessments.

More generally, the Commission services are stress testing the EU environmental legislation to identify significant potential for simplifying administrative tasks and carry out evaluations under the Better Regulation rules4 as applicable.

Furthermore, the Commissioner for Environment, Water Resilience and a Competitive Circular Economy held an implementation dialogue on permitting and environmental assessments in April 2025. The Commission is fully committed to simplify EU laws so that they can be fully implemented.
